An additional endothermic peak for the non-annealed sample was found at 40˚C, which is attributed to the ferroelectric phase transition.27 From the first heating traces (Figure 3a,b) of the non-annealed films, a broad peak is shown from -10˚C to 30˚C for the ES film (Figure 3a) and from -10˚C to 40˚C for the SC film (Figure 3b). This temperature range is known for the Curie transition of PVDF-TrFE-CFE.28 The decrease in the Curie temperature for the ES film suggests that less energy will be needed to orient the alignment of electric dipoles in the ES film than in the SC film. The melting transition for both ES and SC non-annealed films was found near 130˚C. However, the latent heat release of ES film was 19.2 J/g, which is about 36% higher than the SC film (14.4 J/g). Figure 3. (a,b) DSC first heating traces of terpolymer films prepared using (a) electrospray processing and (b) solution casting. The numbers appearing next to the endotherms denote the latent heat of fusion. (c,d) XRD scans of terpolymer films prepared using (c) electrospray processing and (d) solution casting. For all plots, data from annealed films (black trace), films annealed at 60˚C (A60, red trace), and films annealed at 120˚C (A120, blue trace) are shown. Applying thermal annealing treatments to the terpolymer films does not change the melting temperature, indicating that the paraelectric phase is formed regardless of the annealing treatments and film fabrication methods (Figure 3a,b). Both the ES and SC films follow the same trend for the latent heat of fusion: increasing the annealing temperature leads to larger values for the heat of 11 DE-EE0009099 fusion. The increase in the latent heat values suggests the enhancement of crystallinity in the paraelectric phase after higher temperature annealing. The second heating traces for both ES and SC films are shown in Figure S3a,b and follow the same trend as the first heating trace. The enhancement of latent heat from the melting transition encourages the increase of entropy in the system at equilibrium according to Equation 2. ∆𝐻 = 𝑇∆𝑆 (Eqn. 2), where ∆H is the latent heat released, T is the temperature and ∆S is the change of entropy of the system. With the increase of the entropy, the ∆T can also increase (Eqn. 1). X-ray diffraction (XRD) was used to characterize different phases in the films (Figure 3c,d) and to estimate the average crystal size in the terpolymer film. A broad peak shows up for both non-annealed films from 14˚ to 22˚ and indicates the presence of three phases including ferroelectric, paraelectric, and relaxor ferroelectric phases.29 For the annealed ES and SC films, a sharp peak shows up at 18.5˚ and indicates {110, 200} reflection of the paraelectric phase.
